records.title: Attack (1) 1 · Freighter

fields.narrative: with target track of 90° port, speed 10, and range of about 1,800 yards, fired a three torpedo spread. First torpedo, prematured at 20 seconds, second torpedo hit on bow, third torpedo hit on stern. Sound unable to hear screws after two hits. Definitely heard breaking up noises on sound gear. The premature momentarily blinded the periscope. Only one torpedo, the third, was seen to hit, but all hands heard two hits following the premature. The target was surrounded by black smoke. Sighted target with decks awash.

records.title: Attack (2) 2 · Freighter

fields.narrative: fired three torpedo spread with 100° port track, speed of 11 3/4 knots, and actual range of 1,150 yards. All torpedoes were set on 15 feet. The first torpedo hit amidships with a terrific explosion, but the second and third torpedoes missed. The second torpedo was tracked ahead of the screws by sound. The target's screws were not heard after the torpedo explosion. It is believed that the target was drawing less than was estimated and the one hit was an influence explosion. The other two torpedoes probably ran too deep. The draft was estimated at 13 feet and torpedoes were set at 15 feet to run at 12 feet. The target could have had a draft of 10 feet. Although the target was not seen to sink and cannot be credited as such, it is believed that there is a strong possibility a torpex hit amidships sank him.

records.title: Attack (3) 3 · Fr-Pass

fields.narrative: fired a three torpedo spread at each of two leading ships which almost presented an overlapping target. Range to nearest target 1,500 yards; track 100° starboard; gyro angle 011; and range to far target 2,300 yards. Swung hard left at flank speed to clear two after ships, who had a smaller angle on bow, and to try a stern tube shot. Cleared nearest ship 600 yards (by radar) when we were beam to beam. Already had two stern tubes ready and set on 10 feet in case our escort got too friendly.

records.title: Attack (5) 5 · Freighter

fields.narrative: fired two torpedoes while still swinging at overlapping after ships. Total results one hit on nearest leading target (Lima Maru Class); two hits on farthest leading target (Yuki Maru); and one hit on farthest after target (Heian Maru class). These hits were seen, heard, and checked by time of torpedo run. The last ship hit was seen taking a down angle as we retired to southwest at full speed. We had four strong pips on the radar from the four freighters as we pulled away. The escort had never been easy to pick up on radar. He was first picked up during the approach at 7,000 yards. When the range to the nearest target was 3,000 yards, we ran into a rain squall. Heard two distant explosions which sounded like depth charges. The radar officer reported two of the pips getting weaker. Between 5,000 and 7,000 yards, we lost two pips. At 9,000 yards, since the escort did not seem to be on our trail, we stopped. A careful and continuous search over the target area, failed to reveal more than two pips indicating that two ships had sunk. All ships had shown up plainly on the radar screen at 13,500 yards during the tracking. All torpedoes fired had torpex heads which exploded with a terrific noise. The large remaining pip, which was believed to be on the largest ship (Lima Maru class one hit) moved slowly out to 17,500 yards and disappeared. The other pip closed us slowly to 8,500 yards and then opened out and was lost at 13,700 yards. It is believed that this ship was the undamaged one taking a quick look for survivors.

records.title: Attack (6) 6 · Passenger

fields.narrative: with escort passing ahead at 400 yards, right hand ship with zero angle on bow, range 2,000 yards, center ship with 20° port angle on bow, range 3,000 yards, and left hand ship 80° port angle on bow, 1,200 yards, fired three torpedoes (TNT heads) at left hand ship. 1st torpedo jumped clear of the water twice at about 400 yards, just astern of the escort and later prematured, the 2nd torpedo hit, and the 3rd torpedo missed. The escort started turning toward us after 1st torpedo prematured. Went deep to avoid ramming and to evade depth charge attack. Our going under one ship and astern of another seemed to confuse the escort. He dropped four depth charges, but none were very close. The escort then commenced searching with supersonic. He seemed to be strictly amateur.

records.title: Attack (7) 7 · Pass.-Frtr.

fields.narrative: fired three torpedo spread from stern tubes at left hand ship, Nagoya Maru, 6,072 tons, range 800 yards, track 80° starboard, gyro angle 175°. Results first and second torpedoes hit third torpedo missed astern. The first torpedo had a torpex head. The Commanding Officer watched both hits. The time of torpedo run and explosions checked. The ship gave off enormous quantities of smoke, rapidly settled in the water, listed to starboard 15°, and the starboard well deck rail was awash. This ship was loaded well down in the water.

fields.event: with the ship definitely sinking and the destroyer headed in our direction, went deep. Heard cracking up noises for about forty minutes.
destroyer dropped two depth charges.

he dropped two more. None close. The Palau temperature gradient and density layers apparently had enabled us to lose the destroyer at once. A temperature gradient of 17°F. existed between surface and 300 feet. Supersonic pinging and screws were heard until 1103 (I). Decided to take our time coming up to periscope depth due to expected plane search and proximity to channel entrance.

records.title: Blowing negative tank to ascend through density layers

fields.event: started up to periscope depth. Again the need of a silent trim pump was sorely felt. It was necessary to blow out 15,000 pounds of water in bringing ship up from 300 feet. This was done by blowing water to negative tank from #2 and #3 auxiliary tanks and then blowing negative with 200 pound air. Found all clear at periscope depth. Reloaded torpedo tubes aft and pumped bilges. Decided to patrol off Anguar Island the next day in hope of getting a phosphate ship and in order to allow the area off the pass to cool down.

records.title: Attack (8) 8 · Freighter

fields.narrative: fired three torpedo spread from stern tubes at range of 3,500 yards, track of 90° starboard, and gyro angle of 191. No hits. The target zigged away at this time. The first torpedo we tracked out running straight for about 2,000 yards and then it gradually drew around to the right. When sound reported the torpedo screws bearing 243° relative and getting louder, went to 140 feet to avoid torpedo. While passing 100 feet, a torpedo explosion was heard at an estimated range of 1,000 yards. A second torpedo explosion followed in about thirty five seconds at about the same range. The time of run of these torpedoes indicated they had reached the end of their run. This poor performance as regards hits is attributed to the following: (a) Poor torpedo performance. (b) Too great a firing range. (c) Firing torpedo on a "knuckle". (d) Disadvantage of having only torpedoes aft.
